## Consolidated Tickets — filed 2026-08-29

**These 21 tickets replace 130 open ones.** The backlog had grown to 150 open rows, roughly
ninety of which were single-measurement parity findings against nine frames — a shape that
would have cost ninety serial passes on one shared Playwright browser to close nine screens.
They are batched here by **the thing that has to be true when the work is done**, not by the
axis the finding was measured on.

Nothing was discarded. Every merged ticket keeps its row and, where it had one, its detail
section, carrying the `expected` vs `observed` tables the replacement was built from. The
full measurement record also lives in `.claude/plans/parity-sweep-ledger.md`.

**Three rules govern the parity tickets below.** First, **re-measure before fixing** — #74,
#165, #198 and #235 all landed after those findings were filed, and the tracker's own note
said they change the computed metrics of most of them. Close whatever now reports MATCH,
with the evidence in Notes, before touching code. Second, **the change order goes first**
within its frame: #287 in #298, #288 in #299, #166 in #301, #169 in #304 each rewrite the
surface their siblings were measured against. Third, **one frame is one browser pass.**

---

**Added 2026-08-30 by #73 — the focus-ring token fails WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11.**
Measured from the real tokens with sRGB compositing, not estimated:

| Indicator | Against | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ring-clay-400/30` over `stone-50` (card, button) | the offset band and page ground | **1.49:1** |
| the same ring | `stone-0` card fill | 1.60:1 |
| segment `inset-ring-clay-400/30` | its own `clay-400/10` tint | **1.47:1** |
| the search bar's `ring-clay-400/20` | `stone-0` | worse still |

The threshold for a non-text indicator is **3:1**. `clay-400` needs **alpha >=
0.80** to clear it on `stone-50` (3.24:1); at full opacity it is 4.51:1.

This is `04-laws.md`'s own stated ring — `ring-2 ring-clay-400/30 ring-offset-2
ring-offset-stone-50` — so it is on every focused control in the product, and
#73 propagated it to two more components while fixing the rings that rendered
nothing at all. **Deliberately not changed inside #73**: raising the alpha
changes the look of every focus state in the product, which is a design ruling
rather than an implementation detail. Rule on it here: raise the alpha, adopt a
different ring colour, or record an explicit accepted deviation with its
reasoning.

### #316: Lane tooling and preflight test hygiene

**Milestone:** M4.5 | **Priority:** P2 Medium | **Status:** Backlog | **Capabilities:** `core`
**Blocked by:** None

Merges **#256 and #64** — the repo's own tooling; no user-facing behaviour, so no parity gate.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] `laneUp` re-derives `worktreePath` and `branch` when it returns an existing
      `state: 'active'` manifest, instead of handing back stale values (#256). Same class as
      the manifest drift fixed on 2026-08-29 — the fix belongs in `pnpm lane:pr`'s path, and
      manifests are never hand-edited
- [ ] The `packages/preflight` test that fails only under parallel Turbo runs is **reproduced
      first**, then fixed (#64). It has never had a detail section, so the reproduction is
      part of the deliverable

**Found 2026-08-30 by lane 9, which hit three of these in one ticket.** All are lane
or preflight hygiene rather than product defects, so they are folded in here rather
than filed separately.

- [ ] **`lane:up` migrates but never seeds.** Lane 9's database came up with 0 categories
      and 0 tags, so every vendor surface 404s and redirects to profile creation, and the
      first browser pass on #9 was blocked outright with nothing to say why. `pnpm
      lane:exec <n> -- pnpm db:seed` fixes it by hand; `lane:up` should do it. Any ticket
      touching a vendor or search surface is dead on arrival in a fresh lane until it does
- [ ] **The `stripe listen` signing secret drifts from `.env`.** Preflight checks
      `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`'s *shape* and that the CLI is installed, and reports the
      capability green — but the forwarder mints its own secret, and on this machine the
      two did not match. Every locally delivered webhook then 401s, which reads exactly
      like a signature-verification bug in the ticket under test. Preflight can compare
      them: `stripe listen --print-secret` against the env value, digests only
- [ ] **Parallel lanes exhaust the file-descriptor limit.** With three lanes up, `next dev`
      died with `EMFILE: too many open files`, the watcher never started, middleware never
      compiled, and every page 500d with Clerk reporting "can't detect usage of
      clerkMiddleware()" — a misleading error three steps from the cause. `ulimit -n 65536`
      before `next dev` fixes it; the lane's dev script should set it
- [ ] **A malformed body masks a 403.** `POST /vendor/stripe/connect` with
      `content-type: application/json` and an empty body answers **400 VALIDATION_ERROR**
      to a *customer*, because Fastify parses the body before the `preHandler` role guard
      runs. Denial is still correct on every other shape, and no customer reaches the
      route — but a 400 where a 403 belongs is misleading in an audit

### #317: No E2E account can reach a vendor surface — the vendor test user has no profile

**Milestone:** M4.5 | **Priority:** P1 High | **Status:** Done | **Capabilities:** `core` `auth` `e2e`

**Merged as `09618e5` via PR #31 on 2026-08-30, CI green (2m43s).**

**Browser-verified at 1440x900**, signed in as the E2E vendor: `/vendor/dashboard`
renders rather than redirecting, the request row reads `$1,450` with
`expires in 7d` and `Send quote` correctly disabled, the payout gate is absent,
`/vendor/availability` and `/vendor/packages` render, the storefront is publicly
reachable and appears in search, and the customer account is still denied. No
console errors, no horizontal overflow.

**Three defects review caught that are worth carrying forward:**

1. **The seed crashed on the shared dev database while passing in a fresh lane.**
   `vendor_profiles` has unique indexes on **both** `slug` and `user_id`; an upsert
   can only name one, so conflicting on `slug` died on `vendor_profiles_user_id_key`
   the moment the account owned a profile under another slug — which it did, left
   by #9’s own browser pass. **A lane is empty, so a fixture that only ever runs
   there is tested against the easy case.**
2. **`booking_requests_live_package_key` is partial on `pending` *and* `quoted`.**
   Probing for `pending` alone finds nothing once a quote has been sent, then
   inserts and dies on that index.
3. **A request without `finalPriceCents` and `expiresAt` is a row the application
   never creates** — the dashboard renders "quote needed" instead of a price and it
   never expires. A fixture producing one makes every pass that measures it measure
   a state real data never reaches.

**The defect class behind #3, named because it will recur** (and written into
`.claude/rules/db-schema.md` so it reaches the next person editing a writer):
a corrected writer plus an early return over existing data is a permanent silent
legacy. The first fix here made *new* inserts correct while adopting existing rows
untouched, so every database seeded beforehand kept showing "quote needed" for ever.
The guard that makes a writer idempotent is exactly what skips the repair — so the
more careful you are about not duplicating, the more certain you are to strand.
It is the same shape as #307’s `accept` starting to write `booked` while nothing
revisited the rows already written as `pending`, and it does not look like a
migration problem to whoever writes it.

**Deliberately not fixed here.** The fixture produces `stripe_onboarded = true`
with `stripe_account_id = null`, a shape real onboarding never creates — harmless
until checkout (#10) lands. And the branch guard trusts a declared name rather than
the connection URL, so a branch called `staging` is unprotected; pre-existing and
repo-wide, recorded on **#316**.
**Blocked by:** None

Found 2026-08-30 while browser-verifying #307. **Where:** every route under `/vendor`, as the
E2E vendor account.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Expected** | the documented vendor test account can reach the vendor surfaces it exists to verify |
| **Observed** | `vendor+clerk_test@example.com` has **zero `vendor_profiles` rows**, so `/vendor/dashboard`, `/vendor/bookings` and `/vendor/availability` every one redirect to `/vendor/profile/edit` with an empty form. `vendor_profiles` holds 16 rows, all owned by synthetic `*@orla-demo.example` users that the seed never links to the `+clerk_test` accounts |

**Context.** This is not a #307 quirk — it blocks the `browser-verifier` gate on **every**
vendor-side ticket, and the repo's own law is that verification is delegated, not asserted.
#307 was only verified by reassigning a seeded profile to the E2E user directly in the lane
database, by hand, in a script that was deliberately not committed.

A second instance of the same gap rides with it: seeded profiles carry
`stripe_onboarded = false`, so `POST /booking-requests/:id/accept` returns **402 `Finish your
payout setup before accepting bookings`**, and the vendor nav has no `Payouts` entry, so it
cannot be cleared through the UI either.

**Do not fix this inside `db:seed:marketing`.** Changing it changes what every lane sees, which
is how one lane's fixture becomes another lane's mystery failure. The likely right shape is a
separate, opt-in `db:seed:e2e` that attaches the existing E2E accounts to already-seeded rows —
but that is a decision for whoever takes this, not a conclusion of the report.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] A documented, repeatable command gives the E2E vendor account a profile, at least one
      package, and at least one live booking request
- [ ] That vendor can complete an accept without hitting the payout 402, or the fixture states
      plainly why not and how to clear it
- [ ] `db:seed:marketing` is unchanged, or its change is opt-in and off by default
- [ ] `pnpm preflight` fails, rather than warns, when a browser-verification capability is
      required and the E2E accounts cannot reach the surfaces under test

**Tests (required):**

- [ ] A test asserting the fixture command leaves the E2E vendor with a profile and a live
      request — asserting the specific row counts, not that the command exited 0.

| **Expected** | the notification stream connects to this lane's API, or fails quietly once |
| **Observed** | a tight retry loop of `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` against `http://localhost:4028/events/stream?token=...` — dozens of attempts within seconds, on `/vendor/dashboard`, `/vendor/profile/edit` and `/vendor/bookings` alike. The lane's API is on **4020**; **4028** belongs to a different lane |

**Context.** Two separable defects, and both should be fixed.

1. **The origin is not read from the environment.** Every other call resolves through
   `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`; this one does not, which is why it lands on a port no one configured
   for this lane. On a developer machine running two lanes it will connect to the *wrong lane's*
   API rather than failing — which is worse than the refused connection, because it succeeds.
2. **There is no backoff.** A refused connection retries immediately and forever. Beyond the
   wasted work, it degrades every future browser verification: a genuine console error has to be
   found among hundreds of identical failures, and the `browser-verifier` gate reads the console
   at every checkpoint.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] The stream's origin is derived from the same env var as the rest of the API client
- [ ] A refused or dropped connection backs off rather than retrying in a tight loop, and stops
      after a bounded number of attempts
- [ ] Two lanes running at once never connect to each other's stream

**Tests (required):**

- [ ] A test asserting the stream URL is built from `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, not a literal.
- [ ] A test asserting the retry delay grows and the attempts are bounded — asserting the
      specific delays, not that a retry happened.

### #319: Nothing checks that a live route has a frame or a recorded exemption

**Milestone:** M3 | **Priority:** P2 Medium | **Status:** Backlog | **Capabilities:** `core`
**Blocked by:** None

Filed 2026-08-30 by **#306** while ruling on **#80**.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Expected** | every live route is drawn as a frame, or recorded as deliberately unframed with a reason |
| **Observed** | #80 named **five** unframed routes; the count is now **nine**. Four appeared after the 2026-08-28 mapping — `/bookings/[requestId]` (#308), `/vendor/bookings` (#307), `/vendor/payments` and `/vendor/payments/return` (#9) — and nothing noticed |

**Context.** The routes themselves are ruled: `00-README.md` now records four as
exempt, four as needing a frame, and one (`/vendor/portfolio`) as already framed
by `24` and `25` and mis-recorded in the ledger. **That table will go stale the
same way**, because it is prose and the thing that changes is the filesystem.

Parity is the repo's hard gate and it is *unprovable* on a route with no frame, so
a route that appears without one is a screen nobody can check — and it arrives
silently, as four just did. The ledger also disagrees with itself today: rows
36–37 map `/vendor/portfolio` to two frames while finding `S-2` lists it as
unframed.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] A test enumerates `apps/web/src/app/**/page.tsx` and asserts every route
      appears in the parity ledger with **either** a frame **or** a recorded
      exemption naming a reason
- [ ] It fails on a route added with neither — proven by adding one
- [ ] The ledger's `/vendor/portfolio` contradiction is resolved to the frames
      that exist
- [ ] Dynamic segments (`[slug]`, `[requestId]`) resolve to one ledger entry each,
      not one per instance

**Tests (required):**

- [ ] The enumeration test itself, plus a guard asserting the enumeration found a
      plausible number of routes — a scan that matches nothing passes forever.

### #320: `31-content-voice.md` still carries the 48-hour deadline the API contradicts

**Milestone:** M3 | **Priority:** P1 High | **Status:** Backlog | **Capabilities:** `core`
**Blocked by:** Design ruling — a ticket may not edit `design-plan/`

Filed 2026-08-30 while tracing #302 for approved per-tab copy. **Where:**
`design/design-plan/31-content-voice.md`, the **Request reassurance** row.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Expected** | the approved-strings file states the deadline the API enforces |
| **Observed** | it reads *"You're requesting, not paying. Maya has 48 hours to confirm or send a revised quote — you approve before any card is charged."* — the exact literal #216 identified as false. `BOOKING_REQUEST_EXPIRY_DAYS` is **7 days**, and #308 derives every rendered instance from it |

**Why it survived.** #216's acceptance asked that "`31-content-voice.md` carries
one approved phrasing", and **#308 closed without doing it**. Not an oversight
that can be fixed by another ticket: `31-content-voice.md` is `design-plan/`, and
`web-design-parity.md` is explicit that *design passes edit the plan; tickets
write the code, never the reverse.* So the code was corrected and the source of
approved copy was not, because the ticket had no standing to touch it.

**Doubly stale.** #308 also made the sentence conditional. A package-priced
request carries an immutable price, so the vendor's only routes are to confirm or
decline; only a custom request can be offered a quote. The rendered copy now
branches, and the approved string knows nothing of either branch.

**Why it matters more than a stale doc.** `31-content-voice.md` is the file every
ticket is told to take approved strings from, and the Text axis is checked
against it. The next screen to quote it reintroduces a deadline the API refuses —
at the moment of commitment, which is where #216 found it the first time.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] The **Request reassurance** row states the real window, derived from the
      same constant the code reads rather than restated as a literal
- [ ] Both branches are covered — packaged (confirm or decline) and custom
      (confirm or send a quote) — or the row states which one it is the approved
      wording for
- [ ] Any other row quoting a duration is checked against its constant in the
      same pass

**Tests (required):**

- [ ] A test asserting no approved string in `31-content-voice.md` contains a
      hard-coded duration for a deadline the code derives — the same guard shape
      as `one-deadline-one-fee.test.ts`, pointed at the plan rather than the app.
      It is the only thing that would have caught this, since the file is prose
      nothing imports.
